column1: # Shared redaction vectors: tst_core::url::redact_url and org.tstrans.Redact.url must map
# each input to its expected output byte for byte. One row per line, input<TAB>expected;
# lines starting with # and blank lines are skipped.
# A row must not hold a lone carriage return: the Java reader splits lines on it, Rust does not.
# A raw ? before the last @ is password text, even with an = after it.
# Accepted over-redaction: a query value holding an @ is read as userinfo.
# Accepted over-redaction: any later @ ends the userinfo.
# A secret query value holding an @ is redacted through its end, merged with the userinfo mask.
# A non-secret value holding an @ with no colon before it is not userinfo.
# A URL opened right after a quote runs to the last matching quote before the next URL opened by
# the same quote, when that quote is followed by a separator, , ; . : ) ] } or the end; otherwise
# it runs to the end of the input.
# Accepted over-redaction: a later quoted word joins the URL's span.
# Accepted over-redaction: an apostrophe inside a later word extends the span to the end.
# Only a later URL opened by the same quote ends the span; a bare scheme-looking word does not.
# That quote opens a URL only at the start of the text or after a separator, , ; : = ( [ {, so a
# secret holding a quote and a scheme stays inside the span.
# A secret holding a quote, text, then a quote-opened URL: no quote closes the span before that
# URL, so the span runs to the end of the text.
# A quote inside a secret with no closing quote after it does not end the span.

column2:
srt://u:<redacted>@h
'srt://h?token=a'b	'srt://h?token=<redacted>
'srt://u:p'w@h failed; retry 'srt://x'	'srt://u:<redacted>@h failed; retry 'srt://x'
# Documented residual, pinned so a rule change shows here: a secret holding the quote followed by
# a space or , ; . : ) ] } reads as the end of the quoted URL, and the rest stays visible.
'srt://u:p' w@h	'srt://u:p' w@h
'srt://u:p',w@h	'srt://u:p',w@h
'srt://u:p'.w@h: timeout	'srt://u:p'.w@h: timeout
'srt://h?token=a';b	'srt://h?token=<redacted>';b

# A multi-byte character directly before a scheme.
“srt://u:p@h”	“srt://u:<redacted>@h”
ésrt://u:p@h	ésrt://u:<redacted>@h
é://h	é://h
😀srt://u:p@h	😀srt://u:<redacted>@h
'srt://u:pw' rtsp://v:q@c	'srt://u:pw' rtsp://v:<redacted>@c
# The longest secret key fully percent-encoded (36 bytes) is still a key; one more byte is not.
srt://h?%73%72%74%5f%73%74%72%65%61%6d%69%64=x	srt://h?%73%72%74%5f%73%74%72%65%61%6d%69%64=<redacted>
srt://h?a%73%72%74%5f%73%74%72%65%61%6d%69%64=x	srt://h?a%73%72%74%5f%73%74%72%65%61%6d%69%64=x
# A key that starts inside a run of % is still found.
srt://h?%%%token=abc	srt://h?%%%token=<redacted>
